Original Definition: Access control is a set of security measures that regulate who can access a system, services, data, or resource. Access control policies use authentication and authorization to verify users and enable access.
Published Definition: Access control is a set of security measures that regulate who can access a system, services, data, or resource. Access control policies use authentication and authorization to verify users and enable access.
Name: access-control

Original Definition: Accuracy measures the degree to which data describes the real-world phenomena it is intended to represent.
Published Definition: Accuracy measures the degree to which data describes the real-world phenomena it is intended to represent.
Name: accuracy

Original Definition: A listing of application programming interfaces and exchange contracts with metadata, intended for use by a software developer.
Published Definition: A listing of application programming interfaces and exchange contracts with metadata, intended for use by a software developer.
Name: api-catalogue

Original Definition: Organizations that integrate application programming interfaces into their business applications.
Published Definition: An organization, system, service, or application that uses an API to access data or functionality provided by another system or service.
Name: api-consumer

Original Definition: A technology platform that acts as a single entry point for multiple application programming interfaces, managing requests, routing, security, and other operations, simplifying and centralizing API management.
Published Definition: A technology platform that acts as a single entry point for multiple application programming interfaces, managing requests, routing, security, and other operations, simplifying and centralizing API management.
Name: api-gateway

Original Definition: (a) The person named on a land title form as the person acquiring an interest in land. (b) The person named as applicant in the application section is the person with whom land title staff is authorized to communicate with regarding an application.
Published Definition: (a) The person named on a land title form as the person acquiring an interest in land. (b) The person named as applicant in the application section is the person with whom land title staff is authorized to communicate with regarding an application.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: applicant

Original Definition: An Application Programming Interface (API) is a software-to-software interface that provides a secure and standardized way for applications to communicate with each other to deliver requested data without user intervention.
Published Definition: An Application Programming Interface (API) is a software-to-software interface that provides a secure and standardized way for applications to communicate with each other to deliver requested data without user intervention.
Name: application-programming-interface-api

Original Definition: A signed, immutable log entry recording access or transfer events.
Published Definition: A signed, immutable log entry recording access or transfer events.
Name: audit-event

Original Definition: Authentication is a security process for verifying the identity of a user or device before allowing access to a system, resource, or function. Authentication validates that a user or system is who they claim to be.
Published Definition: Authentication is a security process for verifying the identity of a user or device before allowing access to a system, resource, or function. Authentication validates that a user or system is who they claim to be.
Name: authentication

Original Definition: Method used to verify the identity of a user or system, such as passwords, tokens, OAuth, API keys, or multi-factor authentication patterns.
Published Definition: Method used to verify the identity of a user or system, such as passwords, tokens, OAuth, API keys, or multi-factor authentication patterns.
Name: authentication-type

Original Definition: Data located in any repository system that is recognized through governance, law, or common acceptance as the source of origin for accurate data on a specific topic. Authoritative Data may be stored or referenced in a Data Register.
Published Definition: Data located in any repository system that is recognized through governance, law, or common acceptance as the source of origin for accurate data on a specific topic. Authoritative Data may be stored or referenced in a Data Register.
Name: authoritative-data

Original Definition: The publicly accessible list of datasets that are designated authoritative through the corporate data governance process. This information is published in the BC Data Catalogue.
Published Definition: The publicly accessible list of datasets that are designated authoritative through the corporate data governance process. This information is published in the BC Data Catalogue.
Comments: Cross check latest DR Standard definition.
Name: authoritative-data-directory

Original Definition: Authorization is a security process for providing a user or device with access to a requested system, resource, or function based on permissions. Authorization is provided only after a user or device has been authenticated.
Published Definition: Authorization is a security process for providing a user or device with access to a requested system, resource, or function based on permissions. Authorization is provided only after a user or device has been authenticated e.g. IDIR.
Name: authorization

Original Definition: The entity that confirms legal basis, consent, or program authority for an exchange.
Published Definition: The entity responsible for confirming that a data exchange has the required legal basis, consent, delegation, or policy authority to proceed.
Name: authorizing-authority

Original Definition:
Birth Date from the BCSC.
The individual's documented birth date recorded from valid identification.
Published Definition: The individual's documented birth date recorded from valid identification.
Name: birth-date

Original Definition: There are many independent or partially independent agencies, boards and commissions that are essential to effectively governing the province. Agencies include authorities, boards, commissions, corporations and councils. A public agency also includes any bodies established by the government on an interim basis to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions.
Published Definition: There are many independent or partially independent agencies, boards and commissions that are essential to effectively governing the province. Agencies include authorities, boards, commissions, corporations and councils. A public agency also includes any bodies established by the government on an interim basis to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions.
Name: central-government-agencies

Original Definition: A Certificate Authority (CA) is a trusted organization that provides/issues digital certificates to websites, businesses, and individuals. This establishes trust between users and websites by ensuring that sensitive data remains private.
Published Definition: A Certificate Authority (CA) is a trusted organization that provides/issues digital certificates to websites, businesses, and individuals. This establishes trust between users and websites by ensuring that sensitive data remains private.
Name: certificate-authority-ca

Original Definition: The transport mode used for an exchange: Pull API, Push Webhook, Message Queue, Batch File, or Streaming.
Published Definition: The transport mode used for an exchange: Pull API, Push Webhook, Message Queue, Batch File, or Streaming.
Name: channel

Original Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Is a child of a beneficiary or a person who stands in place of a parentWho is a minorDoes not have a spouseIs supported by the beneficiary
Published Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Is a child of a beneficiary or a person who stands in place of a parentWho is a minorDoes not have a spouseIs supported by the beneficiary
Name: child

Original Definition: The proportion of stored data against the definition of “100% complete”. Completeness is contextual to the purpose for data collection (for example, is the scope of collection the whole province or a region?)
Published Definition: The proportion of stored data against the definition of “100% complete”. Completeness is contextual to the purpose for data collection (for example, is the scope of collection the whole province or a region?)
Name: completeness

Original Definition: The centralized repository documenting technical metadata for Connected Services data elements.
Published Definition: The centralized repository documenting technical metadata for Connected Services data elements.
Name: connected-services-data-dictionary

Original Definition: The centralized repository documenting concepts in plain language for Connected Services business and technical terms.
Published Definition: The centralized repository documenting concepts in plain language for Connected Services business and technical terms.
Comments: RJS 02/23: Should this be changed to Connected terms instead of Govt. datasets?
Name: connected-services-glossary-of-terms

Original Definition: Consent is a voluntary agreement by an individual for their personal information to be accessed, verified or used by a government service for specified purposes such as determining or verifying eligibility for other benefits or services.
Published Definition: Consent is a voluntary agreement by an individual for their personal information to be accessed, verified or used by a government service for specified purposes such as determining or verifying eligibility for other benefits or services.
Name: consent

Original Definition: A transfer of an estate or interest in land (other than by will) to a new owner through sale, lease, or other means. A transfer of title is the conveyance of an estate or interest in land in exchange for some financial consideration, typically a sale.
Published Definition: A transfer of an estate or interest in land (other than by will) to a new owner through sale, lease, or other means. A transfer of title is the conveyance of an estate or interest in land in exchange for some financial consideration, typically a sale.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: conveyance

Original Definition: Copyright is an exclusive legal right to reproduce, publish and sell a work or material. Copyright encompasses a wide range of materials including: written materials, such as books, manuals, reports and computer software; visual materials such as videos, photographs, pictures, posters and maps; and audio materials such as music and voice recordings.
Published Definition: Copyright is an exclusive legal right to reproduce, publish and sell a work or material. Copyright encompasses a wide range of materials including: written materials, such as books, manuals, reports and computer software; visual materials such as videos, photographs, pictures, posters and maps; and audio materials such as music and voice recordings.
Name: copyright

Original Definition: A corporation means a company, a body corporate, a body politic and corporate, an incorporated association or a society, however and wherever incorporated, but does not include a municipality or a corporation sole.
Published Definition: A corporation means a company, a body corporate, a body politic and corporate, an incorporated association or a society, however and wherever incorporated, but does not include a municipality or a corporation sole.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: corporation

Original Definition: The two-letter country code of an individual's provided residential address.
Published Definition: The two-letter country code of an individual's provided residential address.
Name: country

Original Definition: A verifiable claim about an actor or system used for authentication or authorization.
Published Definition: A verifiable claim about an actor or system used for authentication or authorization.
Name: credential

Original Definition: Any IM IT service, system, or infrastructure component that is deemed necessary by the System Owner to deliver a Mission Critical Function.
Published Definition: Any IM IT service, system, or infrastructure component that is deemed necessary by the System Owner to deliver a Mission Critical Function.
Name: critical-system

Original Definition: Crown corporations are owned by the government, but operate at arm’s length from the public service and elected officials.
Published Definition: Crown corporations are owned by the government, but operate at arm’s length from the public service and elected officials.
Name: crown-corporations

Original Definition: Land owned and administered by a government, either federal or provincial. In British Columbia, Federal (Canadian) Crown land includes National Parks, Indian Reserves, federal ports and military bases. Provincial Crown land includes provincial parks and all ungranted land (wilderness) within the provincial boundaries. Most of British Columbia is Crown land.
Published Definition: Land owned and administered by a government, either federal or provincial. In British Columbia, Federal (Canadian) Crown land includes National Parks, Indian Reserves, federal ports and military bases. Provincial Crown land includes provincial parks and all ungranted land (wilderness) within the provincial boundaries. Most of British Columbia is Crown land.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: crown-land

Original Definition: The smallest meaningful units of recorded information generated by an organization, which gain significance when stored in a structured manner that enables them to be synthesized and interpreted.
Published Definition: The smallest meaningful units of recorded information generated by an organization, which gain significance when stored in a structured manner that enables them to be synthesized and interpreted.
Name: data

Original Definition: The ability for authorized users to easily find, retrieve, and use data when they need it, supported by appropriate permissions, usable formats, documentation, and interoperability that allows data to work across systems and contexts.
Published Definition: The ability for authorized users to easily find, retrieve, and use data when they need it, supported by appropriate permissions, usable formats, documentation, and interoperability that allows data to work across systems and contexts.
Name: data-accessibility

Original Definition: A data catalogue is a listing of data in an organization (e.g., B.C. Data Catalogue) that is designed to help data users quickly find appropriate data for any analytical or business purpose.
Published Definition: A data catalogue is a listing of data in an organization (e.g., B.C. Data Catalogue) that is designed to help data users quickly find appropriate data for any analytical or business purpose.
Name: data-catalogue

Original Definition: A Data Consumer, in the context of B.C. Data Catalogue, is an individual or group that uses the B.C. Data Catalogue to search for and access datasets. Data Consumers may be internal (within the B.C. Government and broader public sector) or external (public users).
Published Definition: A data consumer is an individual, team, or system that discovers, accesses, and uses data provided by others to support applications, services, analysis, or decision-making. Data consumers rely on clear metadata, quality assurances, and stable access mechanisms to confidently integrate and use data.
Name: data-consumer

Original Definition: For the data assigned to them, data custodians provide oversight throughout its lifecycle; ensure intended users of the data are supported and trained appropriately; and the data meets the requirements of applicable laws, policies, and standards.
Published Definition: For the data assigned to them, data custodians provide oversight throughout its lifecycle; ensure intended users of the data are supported and trained appropriately; and the data meets the requirements of applicable laws, policies, and standards.
Name: data-custodian

Original Definition: The smallest identifiable unit of data with a defined meaning, typically represented as an attribute or field within a data model or dataset.
Published Definition: The smallest identifiable unit of data with a defined meaning, typically represented as an attribute or field within a data model or dataset.
Name: data-element

Original Definition: A governed, repeatable transfer of data from a provider to a consumer under an approved legal basis.
Published Definition: A governed, repeatable transfer of data from a provider to a consumer under an approved legal basis.
Name: data-exchange

Original Definition: The ability for multiple systems to reliably exchange and understand data using standardized machine-readable formats, shared semantic definitions, and common technical protocols in alignment with applicable policies and standards.
Published Definition: The ability for multiple systems to reliably exchange and understand data using standardized machine-readable formats, shared semantic definitions, and common technical protocols in alignment with applicable policies and standards.
Name: data-interoperability

Original Definition: Restricts shared data to the minimum required for the purpose.
Published Definition: Restricts shared data to the minimum required for the purpose.
Name: data-minimization-rule

Original Definition: Data Providers are members of Government Ministries, Crown Corporations and Broader Public Sector agencies who list data in the BCDC. Data Providers may hold one or more roles in the catalogue, e.g. Catalogue Editor.
Published Definition: A data provider is an individual, team, or organization responsible for creating, managing, governing, and sharing data for use by others. Data providers ensure that datasets are accurate, well-described, policy-compliant, and fit for reuse, and they define the conditions under which the data can be accessed and used (e.g., via APIs, data products, or exchanges).
Name: data-provider

Original Definition: A measure of the data’s reliability, including its accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and interoperability.
Published Definition: A measure of the data’s reliability, including its accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and interoperability.
Name: data-quality

Original Definition: Data Quality Assessment Framework defines standardized dimensions of data quality and associated measures for assessing the level of data quality. A measure may apply at the dataset, record, and/or attribute level.
Published Definition: Data Quality Assessment Framework defines standardized dimensions of data quality and associated measures for assessing the level of data quality. A measure may apply at the dataset, record, and/or attribute level.
Name: data-quality-assessment-framework

Original Definition: A Data Quality Scorecard is an instance or snapshot of a dataset’s data quality measures, as defined by the Data Quality Assessment Framework.
Published Definition: A Data Quality Scorecard is an instance or snapshot of a dataset’s data quality measures, as defined by the Data Quality Assessment Framework.
Name: data-quality-scorecard

Original Definition: A set of data that contains Authoritative Data and follows a specific standard to ensure quality, interoperability, and data sharing.
Published Definition: A set of data that contains Authoritative Data and follows a specific standard to ensure quality, interoperability, and data sharing.
Name: data-register

Original Definition: Data Resource (or Resource) for a Data Catalogue is a file containing actual data, uploaded to the Catalogue (e.g. CSV, xls, XML etc.); or relevant information in the Catalogue, describing how to obtain the actual data (e.g. API specification). A data resource is always relevant to a particular Dataset.
Published Definition: Data Resource (or Resource) for a Data Catalogue is a file containing actual data, uploaded to the Catalogue (e.g. CSV, xls, XML etc.); or relevant information in the Catalogue, describing how to obtain the actual data (e.g. API specification). A data resource is always relevant to a particular Dataset.
Name: data-resource

Original Definition: The Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) is a legal agreement defining the lawful basis, permitted use, retention, and custodianship for an exchange.
Published Definition: The Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) is a legal agreement defining the lawful basis, permitted use, retention, and custodianship for an exchange.
Name: data-sharing-agreement-dsa

Original Definition: A Dataset refers to a description (of what the Dataset is about) + collection of metadata elements / attributes / objects + optionally Data Resource(s); where a metadata element / attribute / object is any one piece of relevant metadata for the Dataset.
Published Definition: The structured collection of data for a defined topic, for example an entity, domain, or subject area. Dataset refers to the data, metadata about the dataset as well as optionally associated Data Resource/s
Name: dataset

Original Definition: A platform component that acts on behalf of a provider or consumer, such as a gateway or proxy.
Published Definition: A system, service, or platform component authorized to act between exchange participants to route, broker, enforce, or transform a data exchange on behalf of a provider or consumer.
Name: delegated-intermediary

Original Definition:
Delegation is a secure, formalized process that permits an individual to authorize another individual to access, manage or act on their behalf within digital government services.  
Delegation enables individuals —especially the elderly, persons with disabilities, or those with limited digital literacy—to benefit from digital services without being excluded.
Published Definition:
Delegation is a secure, formalized process that permits an individual to authorize another individual to access, manage or act on their behalf within digital government services.  
Delegation enables individuals —especially the elderly, persons with disabilities, or those with limited digital literacy—to benefit from digital services without being excluded.
Name: delegation

Original Definition:
In relation to another person, it means anyone who resides with the person and who is the spouse of the other person, or is a dependent child of the person, or indicates a parental role for the person's dependent child. 
Note: Adults are not considered to be dependants of each other on the sole basis of demonstrating a parental role towards the same child.

Dependant in the SDPR context refers to a child who lives with the applicant more than 50% of the time
Published Definition: In relation to another person, it means anyone who resides with the person and who is the spouse of the other person, or is a dependent child of the person, or indicates a parental role for the person's dependent child.  Note: Adults are not considered to be dependants of each other on the sole basis of demonstrating a parental role towards the same child.
Name: dependant

Published Definition: With respect to a parent, it means a child, other than a child who is 18 years of age and is a person with disabilities, who resides in the parent's place of residence for more than 50 per cent of each month and relies on that parent for the necessities of life.   In relation to a dependent child, a parent includes but is not limited to: A biological mother or father;  An adoptive mother or father;  A person with legal custody, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act;  A person with legal guardianship, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act OR  A person who is the parent of the parenting dependent child.A client temporarily caring for a child without legal custody or guardianship may also be considered a parent. Caring for a child may include one or more of the following, but is not limited to:making day-to-day decisions affecting the child;having day-to-day care, control and supervision of the child;making decisions respecting where the child will reside;making decisions respecting the child's education and participation in extracurricular activities;making decisions respecting the child's cultural, linguistic, religious and spiritual upbringing and heritage;applying for a passport, licence, permit, benefit, privilege or other thing for the child;exercising any other responsibilities reasonably necessary to nurture the child's development. Note: Under certain circumstance a dependent child may be excluded from a family unit. For example, when two parents are separated but are residing together and the dependent child resides with both the separated parents 100% of the time.
Name: dependent-child

Original Definition: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Older than 18 and younger than 25 years of age In full-time attendance at a recognized post-secondary institution (this includes trade, technical or high schools) Supported by a beneficiary who is the person’s parent or who stands in place of the person’s parent
Published Definition:
A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:

Older than 18 and younger than 25 years of age

In full-time attendance at a recognized post-secondary institution (this includes trade, technical or high schools)

Supported by a beneficiary who is the person’s parent or who stands in place of the person’s parent
Name: dependent-post-secondary-student

Original Definition: Dependents include a spouse, children and dependent post-secondary students.
Published Definition: Dependents include a spouse, children and dependent post-secondary students.
Name: dependents

Original Definition: A document refers to any of the land title forms or supporting material (including survey plans) which are submitted as part of an application to register an interest in land within British Columbia. Examples include: title transfers, mortgages and easements.
Published Definition: A document refers to any of the land title forms or supporting material (including survey plans) which are submitted as part of an application to register an interest in land within British Columbia. Examples include: title transfers, mortgages and easements.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: document

Original Definition: Specific URLs or interfaces in an API or service where requests are sent and responses are returned; the “access points” for interacting with a system.
Published Definition: Specific URLs or interfaces in an API or service where requests are sent and responses are returned; the “access points” for interacting with a system.
Name: endpoint

Original Definition:
Enterprise data is collected, managed, and used across all departments of an organization for planning, operations, and decision-making. It is governed by processes (Enterprise Data Management) to ensure it is accurate, secure, and accessible for business value.   

Enterprise data is listed in the B.C. Data Catalogue, and the listing is limited / restricted to users within the B.C. Government and broader public sector accessed via an authentication method. 

All Enterprise Data listed in the B.C. Data Catalogue is High Value Data, some of which may also be Authoritative Data.

Enterprise data and Open data are mutually exclusive.  However, Enterprise data may be re-classified as Open data at any point in time and as such, will be made available to the public.
Published Definition: Enterprise data is collected and used across all departments in an organization to support planning, daily operations, and decision‑making. It is governed by processes (Enterprise Data Management) to ensure it is accurate, secure, and accessible for business value.
Name: enterprise-data

Original Definition: A uniquely identifiable real-world object, event, or concept about which data is stored. Entities are described by attributes and may have relationships with other entities.
Published Definition: A uniquely identifiable real-world object, event, or concept about which data is stored. Entities are described by attributes and may have relationships with other entities.
Name: entity

Original Definition: Equity is defined as the value of a piece of property (such as a house) after any debts that remain to be paid for it (such as the amount of a mortgage) have been subtracted.
Published Definition: Equity is the percentage of property value remaining after all charges registered against your property and current year property taxes have been deducted from the current assessed value.
Name: equity

Original Definition: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) is a process that extracts, transforms, and loads data from multiple sources to a data warehouse or other unified data repository.
Published Definition: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) is a process that extracts, transforms, and loads data from multiple sources to a data warehouse or other unified data repository.
Name: extract-transform-load-etl

Original Definition: Fee Simple is the form of ownership of real property (real estate) in which the owner has the right to control and transfer the property at will.
Published Definition: Fee Simple is the form of ownership of real property (real estate) in which the owner has the right to control and transfer the property at will.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: fee-simple

Original Definition:
Primary Documented Given Name from the BCSC.
The individual's documented given name recorded from valid identification.
Note: This returns first name only and may not include all portions of the first name.
Published Definition: The individual's documented given name recorded from valid identification. Note: This returns first name only and may not include all portions of the first name.
Name: given-name

Original Definition: A government service is a way for people to give or get something they need. An example is registering a child’s birth or incorporating a business.
Published Definition: A government service is a way for people to give or get something they need. An example is registering a child’s birth or incorporating a business.
Name: government-service

Original Definition:
High Value Data holds significant business value, enabling decision-making in support of programs, services, evaluation, and accountability requirements that benefit a high number of users. This includes data that supports critical services or data of public interest or permanent value (e.g., critical information and authoritative data).

The B.C. Data Catalogue only holds High Value Datasets.
Published Definition:
High Value Data holds significant business value, enabling decision-making in support of programs, services, evaluation, and accountability requirements that benefit a high number of users. This includes data that supports critical services or data of public interest or permanent value (e.g., critical information and authoritative data).

The B.C. Data Catalogue only holds High Value Datasets.
Name: high-value-data

Original Definition: An element (such as an identifier, data structure, or stored record) is considered immutable when its value or state is fixed at creation and does not change thereafter. Immutability provides a consistent point of reference and supports reliable auditing, versioning, and data integrity, even as related or derived information may evolve.
Published Definition: An element (such as an identifier, data structure, or stored record) is considered immutable when its value or state is fixed at creation and does not change thereafter. Immutability provides a consistent point of reference and supports reliable auditing, versioning, and data integrity, even as related or derived information may evolve.
Name: immutable

Original Definition: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals are established by the government to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions. The provincial government appoints at least one representative to these agencies.
Published Definition: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals are established by the government to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions. The provincial government appoints at least one representative to these agencies.
Comments: Need to separate these terms into their own rows.
Name: independent-boards-commissions-and-tribunals

Original Definition: The technical implementation that enables an exchange, such as APIs, connectors, or file transfers.
Published Definition: The technical implementation that enables an exchange, such as APIs, connectors, or file transfers.
Name: integration

Original Definition: A beneficial owner of a relevant trust, a corporate interest holder of a relevant corporation, or a partnership interest holder of a relevant partnership
Published Definition: A beneficial owner of a relevant trust, a corporate interest holder of a relevant corporation, or a partnership interest holder of a relevant partnership
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: interest-holder

Published Definition: As defined in LOTA, this term refers to an estate in fee simple; a life estate in land; a right to occupy land under a lease that has a term of more than 10 years; a right under an agreement for sale to occupy land, or require the transfer of an estate in fee simple.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: interest-in-land

Original Definition: An enactment that provides the statutory framework for the administration of Crown land, establishes the responsibilities of government Ministers regarding the administration of Crown land and provides for the delegation of certain authorities. Many powers have been delegated to the Surveyor General with respect to Crown land definition and disposition.
Published Definition: An enactment that provides the statutory framework for the administration of Crown land, establishes the responsibilities of government Ministers regarding the administration of Crown land and provides for the delegation of certain authorities. Many powers have been delegated to the Surveyor General with respect to Crown land definition and disposition.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: land-act

Original Definition: The Land Owner Transparency Act was passed by the government of British Columbia in May 2019. The first-of-its-kind in Canada, it created an accessible registry of beneficial interests in land in B.C. – the Land Owner Transparency Registry.
Published Definition: The Land Owner Transparency Act was passed by the government of British Columbia in May 2019. The first-of-its-kind in Canada, it created an accessible registry of beneficial interests in land in B.C. – the Land Owner Transparency Registry.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: land-owner-transparency-act

Original Definition: A publicly searchable registry of information about beneficial ownership of land in British Columbia. Beneficial owners are people who own or control land indirectly, such as through a corporation, partnership, or trust. The registry is intended to end hidden ownership of land in BC. The Land Owner Transparency Registry launched November 30, 2020, and opened to public search on April 30, 2021.
Published Definition: A publicly searchable registry of information about beneficial ownership of land in British Columbia. Beneficial owners are people who own or control land indirectly, such as through a corporation, partnership, or trust. The registry is intended to end hidden ownership of land in BC. The Land Owner Transparency Registry launched November 30, 2020, and opened to public search on April 30, 2021.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: land-owner-transparency-registry

Original Definition:
A comprehensive 400-section statute that prescribes the legal program under which the land title system operates, the Land Title Act designates:
•	The Director of Land Titles to regulate land title practice.
•	The Registrar(s) of Land Titles as the primary statutory decision maker(s) in the administration of the land title system.
The Land Title Act establishes the land title register and requirements respecting its operation and records.
Published Definition:
A comprehensive 400-section statute that prescribes the legal program under which the land title system operates, the Land Title Act designates:
•	The Director of Land Titles to regulate land title practice.
•	The Registrar(s) of Land Titles as the primary statutory decision maker(s) in the administration of the land title system.
The Land Title Act establishes the land title register and requirements respecting its operation and records.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: land-title-act

Original Definition: That part of the records of the land title office, including electronic records, where information respecting registered indefeasible titles is stored. It is independently maintained by the LTSA under the statutory authority of the registrars of land titles and in accordance with the requirements of the Land Title Act respecting permanent records retention.
Published Definition: That part of the records of the land title office, including electronic records, where information respecting registered indefeasible titles is stored. It is independently maintained by the LTSA under the statutory authority of the registrars of land titles and in accordance with the requirements of the Land Title Act respecting permanent records retention.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: land-title-register

Original Definition: A unique identifier for each parcel of land in the province. It is a text description that may include lot number, plan number, survey system identifiers (Range, Block, Township, District Lot, District, etc.) and other text.
Published Definition: A unique identifier for each parcel of land in the province. It is a text description that may include lot number, plan number, survey system identifiers (Range, Block, Township, District Lot, District, etc.) and other text.
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: legal-description

Original Definition: Information recorded against a title to land following the receipt of an application concerning matters other than ownership of interests in land, such as statutory restrictions on use (such as the application of a heritage designation bylaw) or rights relating to other land (such as the existence of an appurtenant easement on the title of adjacent land).
Published Definition: Information recorded against a title to land following the receipt of an application concerning matters other than ownership of interests in land, such as statutory restrictions on use (such as the application of a heritage designation bylaw) or rights relating to other land (such as the existence of an appurtenant easement on the title of adjacent land).
Scope: Land Title and Survey Authority of British Columbia
Name: legal-notations

Original Definition: An interest in land claimed to secure the payment of a debt or the performance of some other obligation.
